why:
phase-417 W2.d — `rclcpp::Rate`/`WallRate` is a FORWARDER onto `nros::spin(remaining_ms, poll_ms)`, which DRIVES the executor. That is the class's divergence and it lives on `cpp:Rate` and `cpp:Rate::sleep`; this accessor does not sleep, and its own divergence is the RETURN TYPE.

phase-442 W5 / issue 1331 — upstream returns `std::chrono::nanoseconds`; ours returns `nros::Duration` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:1194`), whose `.nanoseconds()` is the same number `.count()` gave. The reason is the CLASS, not the accessor: `Rate` used to sit entirely inside `#ifdef NROS_CPP_HAS_STD_CHRONO`, so a node written against `rclcpp::Rate` compiled on a host and was ABSENT on ThreadX. W5 measured that the gate was paying for two members out of five and removed it, which means no member may name a type that exists only where `<chrono>` does. Restoring a chrono-returning accessor for hosted builds only would re-create exactly the surface-differs-by-target property W5 deleted.

The porter's edit is one word (`nros::Duration period = rate.period();`) or one call where a chrono type must be kept (`std::chrono::nanoseconds(rate.period().nanoseconds())`). `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_api_adoption_stage2.cpp:273` writes the first and says so at the line, so the probe measures our surface rather than adapting around it.

CORRECTED 2026-09-12: the fix that resolved issue 1331 (`9f600be4e`) wrote this paragraph onto `cpp:Rate::Rate` — the CONSTRUCTOR row — and left this one, the row the filing named and the only row whose signature changed, carrying the sleep-shape reason alone. Both rows now describe their own member.

JAZZY (2026-10-19, `--edition jazzy`): Jazzy's concrete `Rate::period()` still returns `std::chrono::nanoseconds`, but against it the correlator pairs our accessor as shape-corresponding (same arity, no parameters), which is the case `--require-disposition` asks about. Disposition `adopt-bounded`: same value, different type, the difference stated at the definition; `.count()` on the result does not compile here, so a ported file is told.
